newsitem.title: south korea: N.Korean defector dies of gunshot wounds near Seoul.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean defector dies of gunshot wounds near Seoul.

text.p: A North Korea defector to South Korea who was shot by two gunmen died on Tuesday in a hospital near Seoul, a hospital official said.
The defector Li Il-nam, a relative of Pyongyang leader Kim Jong-il's ex-wife, had been in critical condition after being shot on February 15 by gunmen suspected to be North Korean agents.
"Li died around 9:00 p.m. (1200 GMT)," said the hospital official. "His body temperature dropped drastically from this afternoon and his heart began to fail."
Doctors at the hospital said they could not remove a bullet in Li's head because it was too deeply planted. He had remained in a coma until he died.
Li, 36, known in South Korea as Lee Han-yong, was shot outside his temporary home at Bundang, south of Seoul.
Police said the two gunmen were armed with Belgian-made Browning pistols, which North Korean agents frequently use.
The two men were still at large, police said.

Li, who came to South Korea in the early 1980s from Europe where he had been studying, is the first North Korean defector to be shot in the South since the end of the 1950-53 Korean War, according to police.

Police said they suspected Pyongyang had ordered the gunmen to attack Li, to send a strong warning to both Seoul and other defectors following the recent defection of a high-level North Korean official now holed up in South Korea's mission in Beijing.

Tensions on the divided Korean peninsula have intensified since February 12 when Hwang Jang-yop, ranked 24th in the Pyongyang hierarchy, turned up at the diplomatic mission with an aide to seek asylum.
Seoul officials said South Korea would seek to bring Hwang, North Korea's top ideologue, directly to Seoul when it resumed talks on his fate after the funeral of Deng Xiaoping on Tuesday.
The talks were put on hold after Deng's death last Wednesday, with all contacts reduced to working-level, they said.
